newsitem.title: USA: Cool temperatures slow Texas crop development.
newsitem.headline: Cool temperatures slow Texas crop development.

text.p: Continued cooler temperatures during the week ended Sunday helped slow crop maturity in Texas, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop upate.
The update said recent rains had provided for excellent growth in pastures across the state, although the increased growth has also given a boost to armyworm populations.
The cool temperatures slowed cotton maturity in the Plains, and insect and weed control operations increased during the week. The update said rainfall had caused a drop in cotton quality.
Corn harvested 63 percent vs 69 year ago, 97 average.
Corn mature 85 percent vs 82 y/a, 78 avge.
Corn rated 85 pct good/excellent, 10 fair, 5 poor/v.poor.
Sorghum harvested 60 percent vs 70 y/a, 69 avge.
Sorghum mature 66 percent vs 81 y/a, 76 avge.
Sorghum rated 56 pct good/excellent, 36 fair, 8 poor/v.poor.
Cotton bolls opening 35 percent vs 42 y/a, 39 avge.
Cotton harvested 16 percent vs 21 y/a, 20 avge.
Cotton rated 42 pct good/excellent, 35 fair, 23 poor/v.poor.
Pasture and range condition was rated 36 pct good to excellent, versus 29 percent at that level last week.
